title: Pharma Operating Model Evolution and Post-Pandemic Organizational Priorities
summary: Survey-based analysis of how pharmaceutical companies are restructuring their operating models after pandemic-driven changes, including digital capability building, agile adoption, and HCP engagement model shifts.

findings.accelerated_trends: The pandemic accelerated existing trends: digital capability building for virtual HCP engagement, agile ways of working adoption, and cross-functional team structures. Companies already using agile adapted faster to pandemic disruption.
findings.deprioritized_initiatives: Some organizational restructuring initiatives were deprioritized: HCP-segment-based business unit reorganization was put on hold as relatively unimportant compared to digital capability gaps.
findings.digital_commercial_shift: Companies doubled down on digital capabilities for virtual HCP connectivity. This is not just channel addition but organizational redesign — new roles (digital engagement managers), new skills (content personalization), and new processes (omnichannel orchestration).
findings.agile_correlation_with_resilience: Survey data suggests that organizations with established agile practices showed greater operational resilience during disruption. This strengthens the business case for agile transformation in pharma commercial organizations.
findings.operating_model_design_principles: Emerging principles: organize around customer journeys not internal functions, embed digital capabilities in commercial teams not as a separate function, use data-driven decision rights that push authority to the edge, and design for speed-to-decision over consensus.

source: Executive survey on pharma operating model changes and organizational priority shifts influenced by the pandemic
